item.title: Macao ex-legislator jailed for 12.5 years in national security case
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-07
Former Macao legislator Au Kamsan was sentenced to 12.5 years in prison on Friday in Macao's first national security trial at the city's lower court of the court of first instance. Au, 69, was convicted of five charges out of seven, including subversion of State power and establishing links with foreign groups, bodies or individuals to endanger national security, and a breach of secrecy. The court heard that from 2022, Au colluded with multiple foreign anti-China organizations and provided them with sensitive and inflammatory information for publication overseas and online to incite hatred against the Macao Special Administrative Region government and the central government, as well as to sabotage the 2024 chief executive election in Macao. The criminal chamber of the lower court of the court of first instance tried the case on Sept 16 and 18. Throughout the judicial proceedings, the SAR court appointed a defense lawyer to represent Au in accordance with the law, as he did not retain legal counsel. The appointed defense lawyer, who was accepted and approved by Au, maintained close communication and contact with the suspect to put forward his defense. In addition, the court permitted regular family visits in accordance with the law. The Macao SAR government expressed its full support for the sentencing, and called on all sectors of society to respect the rulings of the court, support the judicial authorities in exercising their jurisdiction in accordance with the law, and uphold the tradition of judicial fairness and the rule of law. The government said that it has a constitutional responsibility to safeguard national security. It added that it will continue to strictly implement the Law on Safeguarding National Security in Macao, and will prevent, suppress and punish acts that endanger national security in accordance with the law, so as to ensure the city's long-term prosperity and stability, residents' fundamental interests, and the sustained implementation of the "one country, two systems" principle with Macao characteristics. Following the sentence, the Hong Kong and Macao Work Office of the CPC Central Committee and the Hong Kong and Macao Affairs Office of the State Council published an article on its social media account. The article, written under the name Gang Aoping, expressed firm support for the sentence, saying it demonstrated that national security is a nonnegotiable bottom line. Under the banner of so-called "democracy" and "freedom", Au long colluded with external forces to engage in anti-China activities, severely endangering national security and Macao's prosperity and stability, the article read. "This ruling strongly defends the authority of the rule of law and sends a clear message: anyone or any organization, regardless of what pretense they use or what backing they rely on, that dares to engage in acts and activities that endanger national security will inevitably be severely punished by the law," the article continued. The Liaison Office of the Central People's Government in the Macao SAR also expressed support for the sentence. In a separate statement, the office said it's a vivid practice and important benchmark of the Macao SAR fulfilling its constitutional responsibility to safeguard national security.

item.title: Second China-built cruise ship delivered
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-07
China's second domestically built large cruise ship, Adora Flora City, was delivered in Shanghai on Friday, marking the successful completion of a major national engineering project after 13 years of research and development and eight years of shipbuilding. The project, which involved the construction of two domestically built cruise ships, Adora Flora City and Adora Magic City — the nation's first domestically built cruise ship delivered on November 4, 2023 — represents a historic leap for China's shipbuilding industry toward series production and large-scale development, said senior executives. "Regarded as a crown jewel of the shipbuilding industry, building large cruise ships is an iconic project to test a country's ability in high-end equipment manufacturing, complex system integration and industry chain collaboration," said Xu Peng, chairman of China State Shipbuilding Corp, during the delivery ceremony held at its builder, Shanghai Waigaoqiao Shipbuilding Co of CSSC, on Friday. According to Xu, the vessel's construction time was shortened by eight months compared with Adora Magic City, while its overall efficiency improved by more than 20 percent. "This is not a simple duplication, but a comprehensive improvement in technology management, the supply chain, and talent development, showing that China's large cruise ship research and development has entered a new phase characterized by series production and large-scale development," Xu added. As one of the most complex gigantic engineering undertakings in the global industrial sector, the construction of large cruise ships involves tens of millions of components and parts, thousands of kilometers of cables, and over a thousand sets of systems and equipment. It is a testament to a country's high-end manufacturing capabilities, complex engineering integration capabilities and coordination across its industrial chain. The ship, with a 141,900 gross tonnage, is 341 meters long, 17.4 meters longer than Adora Magic City. It will have 2,130 cabins and can accommodate up to 5,232 guests. Compared with Adora Magic City, Adora Flora City has undergone comprehensive upgrades in spatial design, intelligent technology and the cruise experience. "Thanks to the innovative craftsmanship of the CSSC and feedback from tourists gathered by China Tourism Group, Adora Flora City is more elegant, more technology-savvy, and incorporated with more Chinese design concepts," said Fan Yunjun, general manager of CTG. According to Fan, the vessel is scheduled to make its maiden voyage on November 22 from Guangzhou in Guangdong province, with the aim of offering passengers a new cultural landmark at sea.

item.title: 80 years of efforts chart progressive course of Yellow River
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-07
Eight decades of sustained efforts to harness and protect the Yellow River have greatly strengthened flood control, supported economic and social development, and brought historic improvements to the river basin's environment, officials said on Friday. The achievements have ended the river's centuries-old pattern of frequent dike breaches and course changes, while large-scale soil erosion control has helped turn vast areas of the Loess Plateau from yellow to green, they told a news conference held by the State Council Information Office. Wang Baoen, vice-minister of water resources, said the Ministry of Water Resources and provincial-level authorities across the basin have carried out extensive protection and governance programs under the strong leadership of the Communist Party of China Central Committee. "Over the past 80 years, China has made remarkable achievements in the protection and governance of the Yellow River," he said. A basin-wide system for flood control, rainfall, water and sediment monitoring, forecasting and disaster prevention has largely taken shape, significantly improving the river's overall flood-control capacity, Wang said. The river has also played an important role in sustaining regional development despite its limited water resources. With only 2 percent of China's total water resources, it meets the water needs of 12 percent of the country's population and 17 percent of its farmland, while supporting 14 percent of the national GDP. More than 54,000 projects for water resources management have been built across the basin, while water diversion projects have eased shortages in water-stressed regions. Unified water allocation has also ended the drying up of the river's lower reaches, which have now recorded uninterrupted flow for 27 consecutive years. Wang said continued efforts to conserve water, restore aquatic ecosystems and improve the water environment have put the basin on a path of ecological conservation and high-quality development. The water quality of the river's main stream has remained at Grade II, the second-best level in China's five-tier system for surface water, for nearly four years. The Yellow River was historically known as both China's "mother river" and a source of devastating floods. In the more than 2,540 years before the founding of the People's Republic of China in 1949, it suffered 1,593 recorded dike breaches and 26 major course changes, according to Chen Dongming, head of the Yellow River Conservancy Commission, Ministry of Water Resources. Over the past eight decades, the total length of embankments along the river's main stream has reached 3,000 kilometers. The basin now has 2,768 reservoirs, including 40 major reservoirs, as well as more than 10,000 hydrological, water-level and rainfall monitoring stations. "Over the past 80 years, we have successfully withstood 12 major floods in which peak flows at the Huayuankou hydrological station exceeded 10,000 cubic meters per second," Chen said. "The embankments on both sides of the lower Yellow River remained intact, and the history of frequent dike breaches and course changes has gone forever." Ecological restoration on the Loess Plateau has, meanwhile, helped address sediment, one of the most persistent challenges in governing the river. Yao Wenguang, director-general of the ministry's department of flood and drought disaster prevention, said about 290,500 square kilometers of eroded land in the basin have been treated. More than 60,000 sediment-retaining dams have been built, helping prevent 24.7 billion metric tons of sediment from entering the river. Annual sediment inflows have fallen by more than 80 percent, while soil erosion control has generated 2.43 trillion yuan ($363 billion) in economic benefits.

item.title: China, Gabon elevate bilateral ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-07
China and Gabon upgraded bilateral relations to a community with a shared future for the new era on Friday as part of their efforts to enhance traditional friendship and pragmatic cooperation. President Xi Jinping and Gabonese President Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema announced the elevation of the two countries' ties during their talks at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing. Nguema started his five-day state visit to China on Tuesday, his first since taking office in May 2025. He recently visited Shanghai, where he attended the ongoing ninth China International Import Expo. During their talks, Xi hailed the long-standing traditional friendship between China and Gabon, noting that the two countries treat each other as equals and support each other for shared development. The China-Gabon relationship has withstood the test of a changing international landscape and remains rock-solid as ever, he said, adding that deepening the two countries' ties aligns with the common aspirations of both peoples and the broader trend of unity and self-strengthening among Global South countries. Xi expressed China's willingness to be a reliable friend and partner of Gabon in its independent development, support its autonomy in politics, economy and diplomacy, and work together to build a China-Gabon community with a shared future for the new era. Noting that mutual support is a distinctive feature and political advantage of China-Gabon relations, Xi emphasized that China will continue to support Gabon in exploring a development path suited to its national conditions. China is ready to engage in close exchanges at all levels with Gabon, share experiences in party and state governance, and support it in enhancing its governance capacity, he said. The two nations enjoy economic complementarity and have a great potential for cooperation, Xi said, calling on China and Gabon to strengthen the alignment of their development strategies and cultivate new growth drivers for collaboration. He encouraged the Central African country to take advantage of China's zero-tariff treatment, as well as its "green channel" policy to fast-track customs clearance for African agricultural products, in order to promote Gabon's industrial development, job creation and livelihood improvement and enhance its capacity for independent economic growth. In May, China granted zero-tariff treatment to all 53 African countries with which it has diplomatic relations. Xi noted that his vision of building a community with a shared future for humanity, along with the four major global initiatives he proposed, serves the common interests of the Global South and African countries. China supports Gabon in playing a greater role in international and regional affairs, and is willing to strengthen exchanges and cooperation with it to build a better world together, he added. Nguema said the friendship between Gabon and China has spanned more than half a century, with strategic mutual trust always being the cornerstone of their partnership. Cooperation between the two countries is vibrant, significantly promoting Gabon's economic diversification and improving the livelihood of its people in areas such as infrastructure, energy, healthcare, education and vocational training, he said. Nguema emphasized that Gabon firmly adheres to the one-China principle. He congratulated the Communist Party of China on successfully holding the fifth plenary session of its 20th Central Committee, and said that Gabon looks forward to promoting party-to-party exchanges and learning from China's successful experiences in party and state governance. Gabon is willing to further deepen pragmatic cooperation with China and welcomes more Chinese investment to aid its industrialization and sustainable development, he said. Nguema described China-Africa cooperation as mutually beneficial and win-win, saying that the zero-tariff treatment meets the needs of African countries, allows more African products to enter China's vast market, and holds historic significance for Africa's development. Gabon highly appreciates China's advocacy of multilateralism and its fair and just stance in international and regional affairs, Nguema said, adding that his country is willing to closely coordinate with China to strengthen Africa-China solidarity and cooperation and jointly safeguard the interests of Global South nations. After the talks, the two heads of state witnessed the signing of multiple cooperation documents in areas such as the Global Security Initiative, zero-tariff treatment, industrial and supply chains, and Chinese language education. The two countries issued a joint statement on the building of a China-Gabon community with a shared future for the new era. On Friday, Nguema also held separate meetings in Beijing with Premier Li Qiang and Zhao Leji, chairman of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress, China's top legislature.

item.title: Young Australians urged to forge bonds
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-07
President Xi Jinping has encouraged young Australians to continue promoting the friendship between China and Australia and carry it forward from generation to generation. He made the remarks in a recent reply to a letter from 110 Australian students. In his letter dated Oct 28, Xi said he was pleased to learn that the students had recently visited China for the Sino-Australian Collegiate Rowing and Dragon Boat Friendship Challenge, where they competed alongside Chinese university students, held in-depth exchanges, forged friendships across borders and created lasting memories together. China and Australia share a longstanding tradition of friendly exchanges, Xi said, adding that the future of bilateral relations lies with the younger generation. He expressed hope that the students would continue to promote China-Australia friendship, serve as torchbearers of bilateral friendship and cooperation, and pass the baton of friendship to future generations. In September, 110 students from the University of Sydney and other Australian universities jointly wrote to Xi and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese to share their experiences of visiting China. They expressed their admiration for China's long history, rich culture and capacity for scientific and technological innovation, as well as showed their eagerness to carry forward the bilateral friendship and deepen mutual understanding. During their visit to China from Sept 8 to 15, the Australian students traveled to Nanjing, Yangzhou, Changzhou and Zhenjiang in Jiangsu province. They participated in exchanges with Chinese students, experienced China's intangible cultural heritage, and visited university robotics institutes and new energy companies. "Our time in Nanjing has given us the opportunity to experience the energy of a modern Chinese city while learning about her history, traditions and people," the students wrote in the letter. "We have been welcomed warmly and have gained a greater appreciation for the importance of hard work, commitment and teamwork — values that we share through sport." Chinese Ambassador to Australia Liu Jinsong, who delivered Xi's letter to student representatives on Friday at a ceremony held in Adelaide, Australia, described his reply as "warm and heartfelt, and rich in significance". Daniel Wiersema, a finance and engineering student at Adelaide University, told China Daily that they wrote the letter because they were deeply moved by the generosity of the Chinese people during their visit, and they felt they needed to express their gratitude to President Xi for such an experience. Wiersema said the trip granted them the opportunity to participate in a dragon boat race for the first time, and teaming up with Chinese students allowed them to build lifelong friendships and learn more about student life in China. He noted that youth exchanges were important for strengthening bilateral relations, because "the youth is the future of both of our nations". He added that friendships formed between young people could help foster a lasting relationship between Australia and China. The visit also offered Anja Felderhof, a rower with the Adelaide University Boat Club, a fresh perspective on China. Felderhof, who is studying mechanical engineering at the university, told China Daily that despite language barriers, the warmth and kindness of local people left a deep impression on her. The trip "opened my eyes to a country I wouldn't have thought I'd experience", the student said, adding that she would definitely like to visit China again. Tom Steer, deputy vice-chancellor for student experience and success at Adelaide University, said at Friday's ceremony that the two-way exchange has built "understanding, lasting friendships and connections" between the two nations, and has brought together "learning, culture and the shared experiences of young people". The September event was part of the China-Australia Program for Youth Exchange, which aims to bring 3,000 to 5,000 young Australians to China for exchanges and study tours for three years, starting from 2025.

item.title: Xi casts ballot in Beijing's local legislative election
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-07
President Xi Jinping emphasized the need to practice whole-process people's democracy and ensure the election of deputies who meet the people's expectations, as he cast his ballot in a local people's congress election in Beijing on Friday. Xi, who is also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, voted at the Huairentang polling station in the Zhongnanhai electoral district in Beijing's Xicheng district to elect deputies to the Xicheng district people's congress. He underscored that electing people's congress deputies is the foundation for upholding, improving and effectively operating the people's congress system, and a major event in the country's political life. Xi called for practicing whole-process people's democracy, upholding Party leadership, giving full play to democracy and acting in strict accordance with the law. He also urged stronger oversight throughout the electoral process to ensure that elections proceed in the right direction and in a clean and upright atmosphere, and that the elected deputies meet the people's expectations. The people's congress system is China's fundamental political system, with the National People's Congress serving as the supreme organ of State power. Deputies serve five-year terms, with voters directly electing representatives at the county and township levels. Deputies to people's congresses above the county level are elected by deputies at the next lower level. On Friday afternoon, Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang and Li Xi cast their ballots in person, while Han Zheng entrusted a staff member to vote on his behalf. Hu Jintao also entrusted a staff member to vote on his behalf. Ballots were cast at 13,054 polling stations across Beijing to elect 4,898 new deputies to district-level people's congresses and 11,137 deputies to township-level people's congresses.

item.title: China's progress a catalyst for new start, experts say
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-06
Former British lawmaker George Galloway recalled seeing metal so thin during a visit to a Chinese steel plant that it could be torn by hand. For him, it illustrated a transformation deserving closer attention: China is no longer simply supplying the world with T-shirts and toys, but increasingly with advanced technology. Galloway said China's progress offers lessons for other economies. What some portray as a danger is "the threat of a good example", he said in an interview during his recent visit to Beijing. China's industrial advances are giving other economies access to more affordable technology, new markets and opportunities to develop their own industries, political figures and scholars told China Daily. The term "China shock" is associated with research on job losses and slow adjustment in US communities exposed to rising imports from China. The label "China shock 2.0" is now used in debates over competition from Chinese exports in industries such as electric vehicles and solar energy. Several of the figures interviewed acknowledged that established industries outside China faced adjustment pressures. But they argued that viewing China's advances primarily as a threat risked overlooking the products, expertise and partnerships that could help other economies become more competitive.
